definitions.explanation: The time of year when a business is at its busiest and earns the most revenue.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年末|ねんまつ}→年末：17688_nenmatsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}だ。
examples.english: Year-end is the peak business season.

examples.japanese: ⟦クリスマス→クリスマス：03839_kurisumasu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}だ。
examples.english: Christmas is the busy season for cake shops.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}す→体調を崩す：16480_taichouwokuzusu⟧わけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧はいかない。
examples.english: I can't afford to get sick during the busy season.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{書|か}き{入|い}れ refers to writing entries in an account book. The {時|どき} (time/period) when merchants were busiest writing in sales was the peak earning period, hence the meaning.

USAGE:
Used for any business or industry's peak earning period. Often appears in news and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{年末|ねんまつ}→年末：17688_nenmatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}: year-end busy season
- ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}: summer busy season
- {書|か}き{入|い}れ{時|どき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧: to enter the busy season
